issues.note: "Beaten by a lot" is plain, natural English; the objection is taste.
Item is typical, but it fits a phrase type better than verb + noun.
"Is beaten" does cover records; destroy sense weakly covered. Small point.
Mainly British informal use; a region label means mainly used there.
Intransitive tennis smash (he smashed and won the point) is standard.
"In the last minute" is natural; the alternative is only taste.
Sense 2 covers hitting hard; at most widen the slot to someone or something.
Duplicate of issue 3: the core idea is somewhat weak, not wrong.
Transitivity already records intransitive use; patterns come from a closed list.
